faq.a: A healthy friendship is one where you both feel safe, respected and free to be yourselves. You take turns choosing, listen to each other and make up after arguments.
asks: Tell me about the Healthy friendship

faq.q: What are signs of an unhealthy friendship?
faq.a: Feeling nervous around them, being controlled or threatened, being put down, or being told not to see other friends. One bad day is normal, but a pattern is a warning sign.
asks: Tell me about the Unhealthy friendship

faq.q: How do I tell a friend they are being unfair?
faq.a: Use calm I words: I feel upset when you decide everything. I want us both to choose. If nothing changes, you can step back and talk to a trusted adult.
asks: How do I stand up to a bossy friend?

faq.q: Is it okay to end a friendship?
faq.a: Yes. If a friendship keeps making you feel bad, it is okay to step back politely and spend time with others. A trusted adult can help you plan how.
asks: How do I stop being friends with someone?

faq.q: Is it my fault if my friend is mean to me?
faq.a: No. Everyone is responsible for how they treat other people. You deserve friends who are kind to you.
asks: Why is my friend mean to me?

facts: Experts describe healthy relationships as built on respect, trust, honesty and good communication.
A threat like "do this or I will not be your friend" is a form of pressure, and it is a common sign of an unhealthy friendship.
